title: The process of industrialisation

blocks.heading: The process of industrialisation
blocks.text: Industrialisation is growth in the importance and capacity of industrial production within an economy. It can involve investment in equipment, skills, supporting services and organised production; building one factory does not establish an economy-wide structural change. Industrial production transforms materials into goods, such as food processing or textile manufacture. Greater productive capacity can provide jobs, goods and market opportunities. The development result depends on who can participate, conditions of work and environmental effects. Capacity, actual output and the distribution of benefits are related but different measures.

blocks.heading: An expansion with conditions
blocks.text: In an invented district, processing equipment and training allow more local raw material to be made into finished goods. Capacity and industrial activity increase, which illustrates industrialisation. Whether households benefit also depends on wages, access to work and resource effects. If untreated waste damages water, the output gain coexists with a development cost. Topic 3.1 explains the inputs; Topic 1.1 supplies the wider development dimensions. Use the process definition and a mechanism rather than calling any new shop an industrial transformation.
